text:
marta: seeing a sudden remap growth spike on ap-southeast1 local-NVMe cohort, started ~08:10 UTC. Attach latencies up and a few GPU provisioning requests timing out.
julian: numbers?
marta: remap_rate ~850/s on 9 nodes, attach p95 ~4.8s -> 18s, ~6 attach failures retried. sample dmesg: 
```
[ 2100.123456] nvme0: remap table expand count=4096 -> 16384 metadata_sync=EIO
[ 2100.125678] nvme0: metadata write failed, retrying (retries=4)
```
noah: any config changes overnight? scrub/compaction?
marta: ops-flags show we enabled aggressive KV compaction for benching at 02:00 UTC in ap-southeast1, and scrub-concurrency was bumped to 3 last week.
beth: hmm, compaction + concurrent scrub can cause metadata amplification on remap-heavy devices. immediate mitigation: 1) set kv_compaction.rate_limit=low, 2) throttle scrub concurrency to 1 for region, 3) annotate top hot nodes to pause scrub. cheap and fast.
julian: agree. cost note: cross-region fallback (to us-west) would be ~ $1k/day in egress + preemptible churn, so prefer local mitigations first.
marta: I'm annotating hot nodes now: gnode-501/502/508/517/520/531/540/548/559. command: `kubectl annotate node gnode-501 warehouse.redwood/scrub-paused=true`
(30s)
noah: toggled kv_compaction flag to `rate_limit=low` via ops-flags; pushing a small rolling restart for compactor.
sre-bot: ALERT ap-southeast1 nvme.remap_rate=872/s (9 nodes) incident=INC-20260415-0911
beth: also recommend flipping `scrub-on-attach=false` feature-flag temporarily. reduces attach-time IO.
julian: I'm patching scrub-controller configmap: set `region.ap-southeast1.concurrency=1`. will restart pods in 1m.
marta: monitoring. current attach retries still visible but trend improving.
(3m)
marta: remap_rate down ~65%, attach p95 down to 6.2s. :thumbsup:
beth: good. we should also collect SMART/nvme telemetry for these nodes and correlate with last firmware push (we rolled controller fw 2026-03-29). file STORAGE-821 to track.
noah: filing STORAGE-821 with initial telemetry snapshot and marking nodes for postmortem.
sre-bot: NOTE Attached jobs failed over to fallback tier for 2 Dedicated routes incident=INC-20260415-0911
ops-lead: Ops: notify affected Dedicated accounts about degraded attach window; escalate if any SLA bleed.
julian: plan for next 24h: keep compaction limited, keep scrub concurrency=1, run canary re-enable of scrubs on gnode-548 at +90m, if stable re-enable gradually. also implement a remap-rate circuit breaker in scrub-controller (RFC link forthcoming).
beth: long-term: add adaptive remap backpressure and a metadata write rate limiter in the cleaner path. RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026/remap-backpressure.
marta: if remap bounce returns after canary, we have an intrusive option: firmware rollback of controller group A (impactful) scheduled as last resort. cost ops and coordination required.
noah: agree. log ticket FW-rollback-plan if needed.
sre-bot: RESOLVE incident=INC-20260415-0911 when nvme.remap_rate < 100/s for 30m and attach p95 < 3s
ops-lead: good containment. keep monitoring dashboards and run postmortem if recurrence next 72h. thanks all.
marta: will update status page and incident channel. closing when we hit 30m stable. :white_check_mark:
